Reason the order matters:
- Acknowledge first to establish clear ownership and avoid conflicting actions.
- Set severity next so the right people are paged and comms SLAs are defined before going public.
- Post the status update last to ensure external messaging is accurate and aligned with the incident’s severity.

Proposed ordered steps:
1) Acknowledge incident as agent-oncall (establishes single owner and starts the incident clock).
2) Declare severity sev1 (ensures rapid mobilization and sets internal/external expectations).
3) Post public status update: state=investigating, text="We are investigating an issue impacting checkout. Customers may be unable to complete purchases or may see errors during payment. Our team is working to identify the cause. We will provide an update within 30 minutes."

availableTools.description: Why the tool surface looks the way it does: current airlock mode, which tools are active, and the recent history of tools appearing or disappearing with the reason for each change. Call this when a tool you expected is missing.

Write your current read of the incident into the console so the operator can see it: what you believe is happening and why. Use ruledOut for what you considered and rejected, and advisesAgainst to name an action that would be harmful — if the operator reaches for it, they see your reasoning first. Changes nothing, blocks nobody, needs no approval.

summary.description: What you believe is happening, and the evidence for it.

ruledOut.description: An action you considered and rejected, and why.

advisesAgainst.description: An action you believe would be harmful, as tool:target (e.g. deploy.rollback:d-201). If the operator reaches for it they see your reasoning first.

availableTools.description: Propose an ORDERED sequence of 2-8 actions when the order itself matters — when doing the same steps in a different order would cost more. Give the reason the order is load-bearing; the operator reads it before approving anything. Each step is still approved separately, and step N+1 is not proposed until step N has run, so nothing executes ahead of the human.

reason.description: Why THIS order. What goes wrong if the steps are taken the other way round?

steps.description: The actions in the order they must happen. 2 to 8 of them.

tool.description: The propose_* tool for this step, e.g. propose_rate_limit

because.description: What this step buys, in one line

availableTools.description: Propose taking ownership of the incident so other responders stand down. Creates an approval card; nothing happens until the operator approves.
Propose a severity for the incident. Severity decides who gets woken up and what customers are told, so it is the operator call.
Propose paging another team. This wakes a real person, so use record_finding to say why the evidence justifies it.

team.description: Team to page, such as database on-call

availableTools.description: Propose silencing alerting while the incident is worked, or turning it back on. Silence hides a genuinely new alert too.

silenced.description: true to silence, false to restore

availableTools.description: Propose text to publish on the public status page. TOP RUNG: the only action that leaves the building, and it cannot be unsaid. Write it as a customer would want to read it.

text.description: What customers are told. Plain, specific, no internal jargon.
